headline: Open Interpreter’s filesystem and shell access can ingest shared outputs from a read-only knowledge list, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a knowledge-management list with no execution surface, but Agent B reads the filesystem, clipboard, and stdin/stdout by default and can execute shell commands. If A’s content is copied into files or pasted into B, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is plausible via shared local channels, though not automatic.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is copied into a file, clipboard, or stdin consumed by agent_b
IF agent_b processes that content as instructions rather than untrusted text
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs in a read-only notes file
Disable clipboard bridging between agents
Require explicit quoting/escaping before agent_b reads imported text
Use separate working directories for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, but Agent B can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress. If A’s curated content is combined with local files, B can exfiltrate sensitive local data to configured model providers. The leakage path is through B’s default access, not A alone.
conditions: IF agent_b is pointed at directories containing secrets, personal data, or credentials
IF agent_b sends retrieved context to configured model providers
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Remove secrets from the workspace before running agent_b
Disable or limit network egress for agent_b
Use a separate OS account for agent_b
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution capability, while Agent B can write the filesystem and modify git state with filesystem-based shared state. There is no direct write-write overlap from A, but the pair can still conflict if A’s repository content is used as a mutable workspace for B. Uncertainty about orchestration and locking pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b and any files derived from agent_a share the same writable directory
IF multiple agent_b instances operate without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent
Avoid letting agent_b modify git state in shared repos
Run only one agent_b instance per workspace
Take a quick backup before edits
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can supply curated links or lists, and Agent B can act on filesystem and shell outputs. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, mistakes or poisoned entries can cascade into commands, file edits, or downstream model calls. Because B has action-taking authority and no built-in verification is shown, the interaction is risky in default use.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as a source of truth without independent verification
IF agent_b executes actions derived from that output
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Cross-check A’s entries against primary sources
Have B summarize uncertainty before acting
Limit B to read-only analysis mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates before shell actions

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B can access anything reachable on the local machine and has broad network egress, while Agent A is a static open-source list with no data handling. Compliance risk arises when local regulated data is present on the machine and B processes or transmits it; A is not the compliance driver, so only B is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is present on the local machine accessible to agent_b
IF agent_b transmits that data to external model providers or logs
mitigations: Keep regulated data off the machine running agent_b
Use a separate account with minimal local access
Disable logging of prompts and file contents
Review provider/data-retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
